steps.text: Materials Needed: New Tiles: U, W, X, Y, QU. Known Letter Tiles: A, I, O and all previously taught consonants. Binder paper and pencil, Word Frame, Blank card. Note: QU is taught as a single tile because Q never goes anywhere without U. X makes two sounds (/k/ and /s/ together) but is treated as one unit for spelling.

sections.title: A: Review Known Letters and Sounds

steps.text: Before teaching the new sounds, let's review the ones you learned last time. Which ones are the vowels?
Expected: A, I, and O
Go ahead and tap each vowel's keyword and sound.
Expected: Student taps Apple Apple /a/ /a/ /a/, Itchy Itchy /i/ /i/ /i/, and Olive Olive /o/ /o/ /o/
Tutor points to each of the consonant tiles. Tell me the name and the sound of this letter.
Expected: Student says the name of each letter and its sound.
Let's try a quick warm-up. I'll say a nonsense word, you repeat it. Ready? VUP.
Expected: Vup
Now say just the FIRST sound in that word.
Expected: /v/
Point to the letter that makes that sound.
Student points to the V tile.
Repeat FIRST sound for: WAB, QUIM, YOP. Switch to LAST sound for: TUX, BUB, MIQ (make up /k/ sound for Q). Then MIDDLE sound for: YUM, WAX, QUIG.
Tell me the name of this letter.
Expected: U
Is it a vowel or a consonant?
Expected: A vowel
The most common sound that U makes is /u/. Repeat that sound.
Expected: /u/

Now I'll help you create a picture in your head to make it easy to remember. Close your eyes. Picture yourself standing outside on a cloudy day. Suddenly, you feel a drop of water. You look up at the sky. The rain is starting. What direction are you looking?
Expected: Up
Right. That's the word we want. UP. Say that word.
Expected: Up
The word UP only has one syllable. But we can still tap it. We'll use a hand motion. Point your thumb up in the air and say /u/.
Tutor points thumb up and says /u/.
That's the sound you should make whenever you see the letter U. You say: Up, Up, /u/ /u/ /u/. You try it.
Student points up and says: Up, Up, /u/ /u/ /u/.
Now you're ready to learn the next set of letters.
Tell me the name of this letter and the sound it makes.
Expected: W, /w/ (Keyword: Wind)
This is X. X is special. It actually makes two sounds mashed together: /k/ and /s/. Like at the end of the word Fox. Say /ks/.
Expected: /ks/ (Keyword: Fox)
Tell me the name of this letter and the sound it makes.
Expected: Y, /y/ (Keyword: Yo-yo)
This tile has two letters on it: Q and U. In English, Q never goes anywhere without U. They are a team. Together, they make the sound /kw/. Repeat that sound.
Expected: /kw/ (Keyword: Queen)
Before you spell with those letters, let's run through them one more time. Tap the U vowel for me.
Expected: Up, Up, /u/ /u/ /u/
Now the O.
Expected: Olive, Olive, /o/ /o/ /o/
Tutor points to W, X, Y, and QU. Student says the name of the letters and makes their sounds.
I'm going to make the sound. You repeat the sound. /kw/
Expected: /kw/
Point to the tile that says /kw/.
Student points to the QU tile.
Dictate the remaining sounds: /w/, /y/, /ks/ (for X), /u/, /i/, /a/, /o/.

sections.title: H: Read Real Words with Tiles

steps.text: Now you're ready to take those sounds and blend them into words. Here's how that works.
Let's figure out the vowel first. Tap its keyword, then its sound.
Expected: Apple, Apple, /a/ /a/ /a/
Now touch-and-say each sound.
Student touches first tile and says /w/, touches second tile and says /a/, touches third tile and says /g/.
Next, slowly drag your finger underneath that word while you run those sounds together.
Expected: /w/-/aaaa/-/g/
Now say it fast like a word.
Expected: Wag
Change one tile at a time to build these words: WIG, WIN, TIN, TAX, WAX, YAM, YUM, YUK, MUG, BUG, JUG.

sections.title: I: Spell Real Words with Fingers, then Tiles

steps.text: Now let's do the opposite. I'll say a word, and YOU break it into the sounds. The first word is QUIT.
Expected: QUIT
Now say it again, very slowly.
Expected: /kw/-/iiii/-/t/
Use your fingers to break it into sounds.
Student raises thumb while saying /kw/, index finger while saying /i/, middle finger while saying /t/.
Pull down a tile for each finger, while making its sound.
Student pulls down QU, then I, then T.
To see if that's right, slowly blend those tiles together.
Expected: /kw/-/iiii/-/t/ ... Quit.
Dictate the remaining words, having the student change one tile at a time: QUIZ, WIN, YUM, YAP, BOX, FOX, FIX, MIX.

sections.title: J: Read Nonsense Words with Tiles

steps.text: Now I'm going to build a nonsense word. Figure out the vowel first. Tap its keyword, then its sound.
Expected: Up, Up, /u/ /u/ /u/
Now touch-and-say each tile.
Student touches W and says /w/, touches U and says /u/, touches P and says /p/.
Slowly blend those sounds together.
Expected: /w/-/uuuu/-/p/
Now say it fast like a word.
Expected: Wup
Build these words one by one: YUX, QUIG, VUX, YOD.

sections.title: K: Spell Nonsense Words with Fingers, then Tiles

steps.text: Now you'll spell some nonsense words. The first word is YUX.
Expected: YUX
Say it slowly.
Expected: /y/-/uuuu/-/ks/
Use your fingers to break it into sounds, then pull down a tile for each finger.
Student spells on fingers, then pulls down Y, U, X.
Double-check by blending those sounds together.
Expected: /y/-/uuuu/-/ks/ ... Yux.
Dictate these words: WAM, QUIB, YIF, NOX.

sections.title: L: Read Words Through Word Frame

steps.text: Now you're going to read words using a word frame. If you know that word for sure, just say it. Otherwise, touch-and-say each sound, then blend them together.

sections.title: M: Spell Words with Fingers, then Paper

steps.text: Now you're going to spell words on paper. The first word is TUB. Repeat that word.
Expected: Tub
Say it again, slowly.
Expected: /t/-/uuuu/-/b/
Use your fingers to break it into sounds. Then tell me what letter you need.
Expected: /t/-T, /u/-Up-U, /b/-B.
Make each sound while you write down its letter.
Student writes T, U, B on paper.
Double-check what you wrote by blending the sounds together.
Dictate real words: FIX, WAG, YUM, QUIT. Dictate nonsense words: WUX, YIP, QUAB, ZUX, FUB.
You now can read enough words to read phrases. Read the phrases on this page.
Now let's look at some sentences. Read the first sentence to yourself, then read it out loud.

payload: A bad bug hid in a box.
A fat fox got mad in the mud.
The big yak had a yam on a rug.
A sad pup hid in the tub.
Six pigs bit a cop at the cab.
A bug is in the mud.
The fox sat on a big log.
A man hid the wax in a box.
Tim had a quiz in a cab.

steps.text: How many phrases in that sentence? Mark each phrase for me. 'A bad bug' is the WHO, and 'hid in a box' is the DID WHAT.
Student marks the phrases and reads the sentence with phrasing.
Nonsense words are the first syllables of longer words. Read just the first syllable on your page.
That's the first syllable in the word Public. Say that word. Can you think of any other words that start with PUB?
If the student struggles to think of words, change the directions to: 'Some of these words are real, some are nonsense. Tell me if it's real or nonsense.'
